title: Tenant-tenure failover hysteresis and soft-deny repair
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fix: introduce tenant-tenure hysteresis to prevent rapid failover churn; Fix: soft-deny admission path for short-lived spikes; Stability: resilience to flapping probe results (hotfix).
description: Motivation: during the recent region micro-outage incident (SUP-914) we observed frequent tenant-level failover flips when transient probe jitter coincided with short bursty traffic. That caused unnecessary cross-region failovers and KV cache thrashing for mid-tier customers. This PR introduces a lightweight tenant-tenure mechanism: instead of immediately promoting a tenant into full failover/soft-deny on the first failing health threshold, we require a minimum tenure window (configurable) and an exponential reopen backoff. The change reduces flip-flop by applying hysteresis and a soft-deny admission path that degrades requests progressively (priority trims, queue admission delay) rather than hard rejects. Summary of changes and rationale: 1) runtime/failover: add tenure score per-tenant (sliding window) and a hysteresis timer to the circuit state machine to require sustained failing state before full failover. 2) admission/soft-deny: implement a deferred-admit path that returns 202+progress headers for low-priority requests, applies token-bucket trims, and triggers lightweight telemetry events rather than immediate denials. 3) probe smoothing: health probe aggregator now applies a short jitter-tolerant median filter to avoid spurious flips when probes briefly fail (root cause in control-plane probe burst). 4) telemetry/alerts: add new metric tenant_failover_hysteresis_engaged and update dashboards/alerting to avoid noisy pagers. 5) tests and backport: integration tests added; small hotfix backport to release/2025-11 included. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-1987 - [x] Unit tests for tenure scoring and circuit transitions - [x] Integration test with simulated flapping probes and tenant bursts - [x] Manual canary run against staging (5% regional traffic) - [x] Backported fix to release/2025-11 (manual apply) Rollback plan: revert the head branch, or toggle the feature flag (runtime.tenure_enabled=false). If rollforward needed, increase tenure window and re-run canary. Impact: expected to reduce cross-region failovers and KV churn for tenants with <30s transient errors. This also slightly increases latency for low-priority requests under soft-deny (intentional tradeoff).

review_thread:
Diego: This looks sensible; the tenure window default of 10s seems low for noisy probes — can we make it configurable per-region?
Maya: Agree, made it region-configurable and added validation; default remains 10s for low-latency regions and 30s in high-variance regions.
Priya: Soft-deny implementation is clever, but ensure token-bucket trimming doesn't starve long-tail tails. Request adding a telemetry counter for trimmed vs rejected.
Maya: Added tenant_trim_count and tenant_reject_count metrics; updated dashboards and alert thresholds.
Liam: Tests look good but I hit a race in the integration harness when simulating immediate reopen — added a small mutex around the state transition and re-ran tests.
Diego: CI is green and manual canary showed stable region for 24h with no unintended failovers. Approving.
Priya: Approve, recommend backport to release/2025-11.
Maya: Backportable and validated; manual cherry-pick applied to release branch.

post_merge_followup: Schedule: monitor tenant_failover_hysteresis_engaged and tenant_trim_count for 72h. If tenant-level failover rate not reduced by 60%, revert and investigate further. Ops ticket created: SRE-432 (72h watch).
